voiceover: Five things to settle before you send a single invitation. The Quiet List: before the first invitation goes out. Skip these, and they return as guest questions. Five decisions, in order. Number four saves the most chasing. One. Your A-list and your B-list. Keep friend groups together. Split groups compare notes. A B-list only works if the second wave goes out early. Philadelphia Magazine says: first wave at least eight weeks out. B-list replies due by four weeks out. Two. Your plus-one rule. Decide it once. Spouses, fiancés and live-in partners must be invited. That's Emily Post. Casual dating partners are your call. Apply the rule to everyone. Here's the part people skip: the envelope is the rule. Write only the names you mean. Three. Your mailing date: when invitations go out. For a local wedding, guides say six to eight weeks out. Guests who travel far need more: two to three months. Guides differ, so pick a range and write it down. Follow for tomorrow: your wedding isn't behind schedule. Four. Your RSVP deadline, set by someone else's date. Ask your caterer when they need final numbers. Then count back at least ten days. That's your deadline. Those ten days are your time to follow up. That's why number four saves the most chasing. Five. What the reply asks your guests. Otherwise you'll collect allergies by text, one by one. So add a dietary line, and a phone number for anything severe. Here's the reply page on a Wedillybird invitation. Guests tap I'll be there, Maybe or I can't make it. Then plus-ones, dietary needs, a note. Save this for invitation week. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. Five things, in order. Settle them, then send a single invitation.

caption:
What to do before sending wedding invitations
Five decisions to settle in order: A-list and B-list, plus-ones, mailing date, RSVP deadline and what the reply asks.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
keywords: before you send a single invitation
pinned_comment:
The Quiet List: five things to settle before you send a single invitation.
1) Your A-list and B-list (a B-list needs an early first wave)
2) Your plus-one rule, and an envelope that matches it
3) Your mailing date (guides say six to eight weeks for a local wedding, more for travelers)
4) Your RSVP deadline: your caterer's headcount date, minus at least ten days
5) What the reply asks: one line for dietary needs, a phone number for anything severe
Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: Which of the five did you almost forget?

sources.fact: Send A-list invitations at least eight weeks out; B-list invitations as soon as RSVPs show room, with a reply deadline no later than four weeks before the wedding; keep friend and work groups together
sources.title: Here's Everything You Need to Know About (Tactfully) Inviting Your B-List Guests

sources.fact: B-list invitations go out only after RSVPs show there is room; the aim is that every guest feels like an A-lister

sources.title: Business Insider article via Yahoo (title not recorded in the fact bank)

sources.fact: Spouses, fiance(e)s and live-in partners must be invited; casual dating partners who do not live together need not be
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

sources.fact: Limit plus-ones to married or long-term couples and apply the rule fairly
sources.title: Who Has a Say in the Wedding Guest List?

sources.fact: To signal no plus-one, write only the invited guest's name on the envelope; name every household member you mean
sources.title: Wedding Invitation Wording: A Complete How-To Guide

sources.fact: Local weddings: invitations about six to eight weeks out; destination about two to three months; guests booking international travel usually need at least three months
sources.title: How to Set Perfect Wedding RSVP Deadlines

sources.fact: Mail invitations about six to eight weeks ahead, with the reply-by date at least three weeks before the wedding; Zola's own pages differ on timing
sources.title: Wedding Invitation Wording: A Complete How-To Guide

sources.fact: Venues and caterers typically need final headcounts one to two weeks before the wedding; set the RSVP deadline at least ten days before that headcount date so there is time to chase
sources.title: How to Set Perfect Wedding RSVP Deadlines

sources.fact: Ask about allergies with a specific line (Please note any food allergies or dietary restrictions); give a direct contact for anything severe
sources.title: 25 Must-Ask Wedding RSVP Questions
